CIRCUITS

Electric current is the rate of charge flow. One ampere is one coulomb per second.
Ohm's law says the voltage across a resistor is V = IR at constant temperature.
Resistance is the ratio R = V/I; its unit is the ohm.
In a series circuit the same current flows through every element.
In a parallel circuit the same voltage appears across every branch.
Electrical power is P = VI; it is also I squared R and V squared over R.
A node is a junction where two or more circuit elements meet.
The reference node is the node chosen as zero volts.
Kirchhoff's current law says the currents leaving a node sum to zero.
Nodal analysis writes Kirchhoff's current law at every non-reference node.
A voltage source between two non-reference nodes creates a supernode.
A supernode lets one write a single equation around the source instead of treating both terminals separately.
The supernode does not apply when one terminal is the reference node; then the source directly fixes one node voltage.
A Norton source is a current source in parallel with a resistance.
A Thevenin source is a voltage source in series with a resistance.

THERMODYNAMICS

A control volume is a fixed region in space through which mass and energy can flow.
The first law for a control volume balances energy entering, energy leaving, and the change of energy inside.
A steady-flow device has no change in stored mass or stored energy with time.
The steady-flow energy equation is often written with enthalpy, kinetic energy, potential energy, heat, and work terms.
Sign convention: heat added to the system is positive, and work done by the system is positive.
A turbine extracts work from a flowing fluid.
A compressor adds work to a flowing fluid.
A nozzle converts pressure energy into kinetic energy.
The steady-flow equation fails during startup and shutdown, when stored energy changes.
A closed system has fixed mass but may exchange heat and work with its surroundings.
Specific heat at constant pressure and specific heat at constant volume are different for a gas.

MATERIALS

A vacancy is an empty lattice site in a crystal.
The equilibrium vacancy concentration increases with temperature.
The Arrhenius form gives the vacancy concentration as an exponential of formation energy over thermal energy.
Diffusion is net atom motion down a concentration gradient.
Fick's first law says the diffusion flux is proportional to the negative concentration gradient.
The diffusion coefficient increases with temperature in an Arrhenius form.
Interstitial diffusion is usually faster than substitutional diffusion because the migrating atom is smaller.
Grain boundaries can act as fast diffusion paths.
Fick's first law assumes steady state; it does not describe a concentration that changes with time.
A dislocation is a line defect, not a point defect.
